label: Delimiter step of long sequences starting with d/i/b/o/r/p/h/f/m
explanation: Fires mostly at the <DEL> step (78% of activation mass; never in the copy phase), where the first token is about to be output. Rate rises steeply with sequence length (L=9 > L=8 >> short L) and is strongly modulated by the first original token: d, i, b, o, r, p, h, f, m give 3-6x lift. The remaining ~22% of mass is at the last 1-2 original-phase steps of long sequences, nearly always on first occurrences of tokens (t, c, 1, n, z most often), where it acts as a weaker lead-in to the delimiter activation. Only ~10% of all delimiter steps fire, and the first-token/length rule leaves both precision (~0.44) and recall (~0.51) incomplete. The residual looks like a graded dependence on the token makeup of the whole sequence that simple token-set conditions do not capture. Never fires at t<=2 or in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: d, i, b, o, h, r; least: w, n, c, t) and the next token to output (most: o, r, f, p, d, i; least: w, t, c, 1); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, t=7, t=8.
